From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: lumiere

French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Middle French lumiere f, from Old French lumiere f, from Late Latin lūmināria f (“light”), neuter plural of lūmināre n (“star”) become feminine, ultimately from Latin lūmen n. Doublet of luminaire m.

Compare Occitan lumenaria f and Italian luminaria f.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ly.mjɛʁ/
  • Audio (France (Paris)); “la lumière”:(file)
  • Audio (Canada (Shawinigan)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Paris)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Lyon)):(file)

Noun

[edit]

lumière f (plural lumières)

  1. light
  2. (anatomy) lumen
  3. (Quebec, informal, usually in the plural) traffic light
    Synonyms: feu de circulation (Quebec), feu tricolore
  4. (Quebec, informal, usually in the plural) headlight; headlamp
    Synonym: phare

Antonyms

[edit]
  • obscurité f
  • ténèbre f

Derived terms

[edit]
  • à la lumière de
  • faire la lumière
  • lumière blanche
  • lumière cendrée
  • mettre en lumière
  • siècle des Lumières m
  • vitesse de la lumière f

Descendants

[edit]
  • Haitian Creole: limyè
